name: hero
description: The first screen, as the website actually renders it. A full-bleed stage with media behind it, a scrim over that, and the copy on top — and it is the one place on any surface where the page's inks do not apply, because text over a photograph has no measurable contrast. Two things make that text readable and both are parts of this unit rather than decisions at a call site: the scrim, and a text-shadow on every line. On the site this was a section with four ids, five hand-written rules and a scrim spelled as three stacked `color-mix` stops.

base.$description: `min-block-size: 85vh` and flex-centred, matching the site exactly. `isolation: isolate` is what lets the media sit at a negative z-index without escaping behind the page.

media.$description: Where a `media` unit goes. The hero does not own a video — it owns a hole that one fits into, which is what lets the same hero sit over a photograph or a loop.

scrim.$description: Stronger at the top and bottom, lighter through the middle where the scene reads — enough to carry white text, not enough to flatten the picture. Three named stops rather than three `color-mix` calls at a call site.

heading.$description: `clamp` rather than breakpoints — a hero headline has one job at every width, and three step changes on the way down is three chances to break a line badly. The text-shadow is not decoration: it is the second half of the contrast guarantee, and it is what keeps the line readable on a frame the scrim alone cannot carry. A heading that names the product should use the LOGO's own wordmark rather than retyping it: `avenCEO` set in the body face beside a display headline is two different avenCEOs on one screen. The `logo` leaf goes inline via `logo--wordmark`, and the size rule below is what makes it sit at the headline's own size instead of the logo's default.

helper.$description: The third line — quieter still, and the one most often forgotten when a hero is rebuilt by hand.

heading-mark.$description: The wordmark, inline in the headline. `font-size: inherit` so it grows with the `clamp` above it rather than staying at the logo's own 1.4em, and `vertical-align: baseline` so the two faces sit on one line rather than the display face riding high.

ground.$description: A hero without media still needs its own ground, or the light ink lands on the page.

reducedMotion.$description: The video goes and its own poster frame takes its place — the stage stays, so nothing is lost. Never `display:none` on the media without a ground behind it, or the hero becomes light ink on white.

a11y.note: The `<h1>`, once per page, and it is what names the section. The video is decorative: `aria-hidden`, muted, and it must not be the only thing carrying meaning. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the video is replaced by its poster rather than removed — removing it would take the ground with it and leave light text on a white page. Contrast here cannot be measured automatically: the scrim is the guarantee, and it is why it is a part of the unit rather than a decision at the call site.
